Across rounds 7-9 this prompt grew to ~120 words juggling mask lighting + explicit rotation geometry + head-size proportions, while EVERY accepted root in this manifest uses a SHORT identity-only prompt with style carried by the params and the chain. The extra instruction crowded out the style. This round returns to the proven shape: short identity prompt, one brief framing clause (as the classless entry has) instead of the rotation paragraph, no head-size clause, initImageStrength back to 70 (the value that held style best across the whole roster). GENERAL RULE FOR THIS CATEGORY: when a player entry drifts off-style, SHORTEN the prompt before adding anything to it — accumulated fixes are themselves a failure mode. Fix proportions with the deterministic retouch script, not with more prompt words. ROUND 11 — PERSPECTIVE, ROOT CAUSE FOUND. User: the accepted r10 sprite is 'almost right but the face is turned toward the camera where it should face right'. DIAGNOSIS: a FEATURELESS OVAL MASK CARRIES NO FACING INFORMATION. Every other class signals its turn through head geometry (hood cavity, angled helm front, the Slinger's painted eye); a blank oval has no front, so the head defaults to face-on however hard the prompt pushes 'south-east' — which is why this entry alone kept regressing on perspective while the Squire's helm fix held. TWO CHANGES: (1) initImage switched from classless.png to cadence.png @ 90 — an initImage asserts structure that negatives cannot outvote, which has been the enemy all session; here it is the TOOL, because the accepted Striker already has exactly the 3/4 turn we want, so it asserts the pose while the prompt supplies the red robe and mask. Watch for Striker identity bleed (grey/brown palette, shoulder guards) and drop toward 70 if it shows. (2) The mask is now described with a front: offset toward the right of the head, seen at a three-quarter angle, right edge lit and left side shaded, so it reads as a turned face rather than a flat disc; 'mask facing the viewer' and 'flat round mask' added as negatives. GENERAL RULE: chain from whichever accepted sibling already has the property you keep failing to get — the chain is a structure lever, not just a style lever.
